parts:
Hi all,

I am using methRead funtion to read bismarkcoverage outpout files from bismark alignment.
I don't know why but the function worked well the first time I used it but since It keep returning error even with the same samples :

File '/tmp/RtmpXnwNnv/Sample7_CpG.bed..bismark.cov.' has size 0. Returning a NULL data.frame.
 Show Traceback
Error in `[.data.frame`(df, , 5) : undefined columns selected

The bismark coverage files have <chromosome> <start position> <end position> <methylation percentage> <count methylated> <count unmethylated> format instead of what you what you've put on your documentation : chr, start, end, number of cytosines (methylated bases) and number of thymines (methylated bases).
If the problem is in the format, so why it worked at first and then keep returning error ?

I have already checked on forums and asked questions to solve this problem but I didn't find anything.
I now don't know what to do ... and I am stacked.

I WOULD BE GRATEFULL IF YOU COULD HELP

This is my r code :

```{r}
file.list = list("~/mypath/Sample7_CpG.bed.gz.bismark.cov.gz",
                    "~/mypath/Sample8_CpG.bed.gz.bismark.cov.gz")
```

```{r}
C6.CG = methRead(file.list,
              sample.id= list("Sample7", "Sample8"),
              header = F,
              assembly="AGPv34",
              dbtype = NA,
              treatment = rep(0, 2),
              mincov = 1,
              context = "CpG",
              pipeline = "bismarkCoverage")
```

With the best,

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: methRead using bismark covearge files --> failed
parts:
Hi Mamadou,

I tested with your data on two different machines now (mac and linux) and on both machines it worked fine with the files you uploaded. 

Furthermore the error "File '/tmp/RtmpIDEBx8/Sample7_CHG.' has size 0. Returning a NULL data.frame." indicates that the uncompressed file is empty,
Are you sure that the files you are processing are not empty?

When I was testing your command multiple times I saw that the timestamps of the uncompressed files in my temp folder did not change, 
so it is possible that, when running the uncompression multiple times the files are not overwritten. 
If this is the case, and the uncompression failed the first time, the files won't be updated. 
You could try to remove the files from the temp folder and retry. 

Another possibilty is that the uncompression is silently failing and thereby the output will always be empty. 

To mitigate the compression issues, you could uncompress yourself and use the uncompressed files as input for methRead.

Please let me know wether this works. 

Best,
Alex
